sources.title: Applying for a completion certificate
sources.verified_claim: Higher-risk building completion certificates require a specific application, agreed documents and regulator inspection; a certificate is issued only if compliance requirements are satisfied.

sources.title: Building regulations approval: How to apply
sources.verified_claim: Full-plans approval, building notices and regularisation are distinct routes; completion certification follows completed compliant work and is not implied by application existence.

sources.title: Building control approval for higher-risk buildings
sources.verified_claim: Higher-risk buildings need regulator approval and completion certification; the regime is project-specific and does not establish candidate completion status.

sources.title: Manage a building control application for a higher-risk building
sources.verified_claim: The service supports changes, commencement notices and completion-certificate applications; service capability is not evidence that a sample parcel has an application or certificate.

sources.title: Building control applications
sources.verified_claim: Enfield distinguishes full plans, building notices, regularisation and reversion and states a completion certificate is issued when work is satisfactorily completed.

sources.title: Building control
sources.verified_claim: Enfield provides application search and lost-completion-certificate routes; exact property and application references remain necessary for evidence.

sources.title: Check the progress of a building control application
sources.verified_claim: Havering offers property/reference-based tracking of building-control applications; tracker availability or an application record is not a completion certificate.

sources.title: Completion certificates
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth issues certificates only for applications it handled after works are complete and inspections conclude compliance; copies require identification of the original application.
